note: The ratchet of `pnpm check:coverage` (DEC-0141). `max` is the worst tally this repository is allowed to have. A run worse than a number here fails; a run better than one fails too, asking for the number to be lowered in the same commit, so that a gain is recorded instead of left as budget to spend again. Raising a number is a governance change: it needs a decision record, and the record says which criteria were let go and why.
measured_on: The merge of T-17 (DEC-0136/DEC-0142) into next-2026, which already carried T-21 (DEC-0140). Both sides moved the tally and the merge keeps both movements: T-21 closed TS-WEB-0010-A4 with a walk of its own instead of a comment (MISSING 149 → 148), and T-17's copy-lint tests closed two more by naming TS-WEB-0006-A8 and TS-WEB-0029-A15 in their titles. T-17's one raise stands and is the governance case DEC-0141 asks for: NAMED ONLY 31 → 32 lets TS-WEB-0018-A7 go, because the criterion is not met on the render — /rechtliches and /en/legal carry the product name seven times out of the verbatim legal import — and round 3's VERIFIED came only from a unit-test title. A7 is now NAMED ONLY, which is what it is. The criterion itself is the spec owner's: CONF-0027 (direct_contradiction, OPEN, NEW_VERSION) and state/open.md row 278. Recorded in DEC-0142 §9. The merge closes one MISSING more than either branch alone (146 and 148 → 145), because T-17 and T-21 each name a criterion the other does not; the gain is recorded here rather than left as budget.
